tests/onlineRecovery.test.ts L254-263 builds an active hosted run (reconnect then rehost), clears the mocks, then calls `void suspend(); void resume();` without awaiting. It asserts invalidateLease ['suspended','service-fenced'], dispose called once and join called once. The trace matches the code. suspend (onlineSession.ts L573) queues 'suspended' and then savedState→retireGame, which synchronously queues 'service-fenced' (L175) and clears c.host. resume (L578) sees no c.host, so no 'resumed' is queued, and it reconnects exactly once (L580). The finding predicted 'resumed', but the test pins the actual, safe ordering, so the risk is covered. The response explains 'service-fenced' as coming from the rejoin. In fact the synchronous retire on suspend queues it, as the test's own comment says. The difference does not change what the test covers.
